verses.1: And Shemuel said to Shaul, “The LORD has sent me to be your king over your people, over Israel. Now listen to the words of the LORD.”
verses.2: Thus said Jehovah, the God of hosts: “I have punished Amalek for what he did to Israel. He placed obstacles in the way of Israel when they were coming out of Egypt.”
verses.3: Now go and take revenge on Ammon. Destroy everything that belongs to him. Do not be afraid of him. From the high-ranking officials down to the lowest ones, from the rich men down to the poor people, everyone will die.
verses.4: And Shaul heard the people’s voices. He gathered them together in a crowd of ten thousand men. And he made every Jewish man into one group.
verses.5: And Shaul came to the city of Amalek, and he multiplied the wells there.
verses.6: And Shaul said to Kain, “Go away from Amalek! Do not stay among his people. Otherwise, I will gather against you all the people of Israel, along with their wives who were taken captive from Egypt.” So Kain left Amalek.
verses.7: And Sheol took Amalek away from Hivla, by the gate that is on the face of Egypt.
verses.8: And he destroyed Aggag of Amalek, along with all the other people who were black-skinned.
verses.9: And Shaul and the people took care of the fields, as well as the sheep and cattle in the morning and at night. They also took care of all the good things that existed there. But the plagues did not spare them; all their work was destroyed and lost.
verses.10: And the words of Jehovah were addressed to Shemuel, as follows:
verses.11: I was comforted, for I had made Shaul king. But he did not keep my words. He turned against Shemuel and cried out to Jehovah all night long.
verses.12: And Shmulai looked up at Sheol in the morning. He said to Shmulai, “O Sheol, the vineyard is here! Look, a hand is raised against me; it will strike me and carry me away.” And the ladder descended.
verses.13: And Shemuel went to Shaul. He said to him, “Blessed be you, O Shaul! I have done what Jehovah commanded me to do.”
verses.14: And Shmu’el said, “What is the sound of this sheep’s cry in my ears? It’s the sound of the morning, which I hear.”
verses.15: And Shaul said to Amalek: “Bring them here. Let the people rest well during the day and at night, so that they may offer sacrifices to Jehovah your God.”
verses.16: And Shemuel said to Shaul, “Hurry up! I will tell you what the Lord has spoken to me this morning.” Then he spoke to him.
verses.17: And Shemuel said, “Are you really so insignificant in your own eyes? You are the leader of Israel. But Jehovah will make you king over Israel.”
verses.18: And Jehovah will send you in a certain way. He will say to you, “You have defeated Amalek. You will fight against him until they are completely destroyed.”
verses.19: And why didn’t you hear the voice of the LORD? You turned away from Him and did evil in the eyes of the LORD.
verses.20: And Shaul said to Samuel, “I have heard the voice of the LORD. I will go along the path that the LORD has assigned me to. I will bring back the king of Ammon, and I will destroy Ammon.”
verses.21: And the people took some sheep from the flock. In the morning, they offered them as an offering to Jehovah your God in the wilderness.
verses.22: And Shmuel said, “I desire to serve the LORD through offerings and sacrifices.” When he heard the voice of the LORD, he saw that it was good to listen to the LORD’s words.
verses.23: For Kessam Meri and Aon have sinned, and their sins have caused God’s words to be disregarded. Therefore, they have offended you as your king.
verses.24: And Shaul said to Shemuel, “I have sinned, for I have transgressed against the LORD’s commands. I feared the people, and I listened to their voices.”
verses.25: And now, let me confess my sins. Please come back with me and I will worship the LORD.
verses.26: And Shemuel said to Shaul, “I will not return with you. For you have disobeyed the words of Jehovah. Therefore, Jehovah has punished you for being king over Israel.”
verses.27: And Shemuel decided to go. He strengthened his wing and flew away.
verses.28: And Shemuel said to him, “Today, Jehovah will take away the kingdom of Israel from you. It will be given to your enemy.”
verses.29: And even Israel’s eternal existence will not be deceived or comforted. For it is not a human being who can comfort others.
verses.30: And he said, “I have sinned. Now, please forgive me. Turn away from my people and from Israel. Come back to me, and I will worship You, God.”
verses.31: And Shemuel went after Shaul. And Shaul bowed down to Jehovah.
verses.32: And Shmu’el said, “Bring Agag before me, king of Amalek.” So Agag went to him. Agag said, “I am now freed from the power of the dead.”
verses.33: And Shemuel said, “Just as women destroyed your city, so too will your mother’s daughters destroy you. Then Shemuel placed the ark in front of Jehovah in the valley.”
verses.34: And Shemuel the Rammatah went, and Shaul went to his house in Gibeah Sha’ul.
verses.35: And Shmuel did not see Shaul until the day of his death. Shmuel mourned for Shaul, and God comforted him, as He appointed Shaul to rule over Israel.
